target.title: Attempt on Positive-temperature crystalline Gibbs phases for three-dimensional Riesz gases
target.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Source-specific calculation, conditional implication or exact obstruction Result: The harmonic phonon calculation around an assumed crystal has infrared displacement variance proportional to integral over |k|<1 of |k|^-2 dk. In dimension d this is a constant times integral from0 to1 of r^(d-3)dr, finite in d=3 and logarithmically divergent in d=2. Therefore the elementary infrared objection to positional order is absent in three dimensions. Check: The radial Jacobian r^(d-1) produces the exponent d-3. This only checks the Gaussian approximation conditional on a lattice; it neither selects a lattice nor constructs an infinite-volume Gibbs measure. Obstruction: One must control defects, anharmonic fluctuations and alternative configurations uniformly in volume and show nontrivial positional order. Finite variance within an assumed crystal cannot prove that the full Gibbs law is crystalline. Numerical BCC/FCC phase diagrams are not a proof.

gaussian.title: Technique: Concentric Decomposition of the 2D Gaussian Free Field
gaussian.body:
TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). The concentric decomposition (Biskup-Louidor) describes the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field h in a box of side N as seen from a point x where the field is near its maximum. Around x one takes nested dyadic annuli; conditioning on the values of h on the boundaries of the concentric boxes, the Gibbs-Markov property splits h into (i) a random walk S_k along the scales, whose increments are the Gaussian binding fields' values at x, with variance of order g log 2 per scale, with the maximum constraint acting as a barrier the walk must stay below (entropic repulsion), (ii) independent zero-boundary fields in the annuli, and (iii) explicit bounded error terms from the non-exact scale invariance of the lattice Green function. The maximum-at-x event becomes a ballot-type event for the walk S_k, handled by random-walk-below-a-barrier estimates, which yield tightness of the centred maximum, the local limit law of the maximum, and the description of the cluster of near-maximal points around x (the cluster law nu). It is the tool behind the full extremal process of the DGFF (Biskup-Louidor 2016, 2018) and the intermediate level sets. It does not by itself give universality for other log-correlated fields: the binding-field structure uses the DGFF's exact Gibbs-Markov property. Typical failure: Treating the annulus fields phi_k as exactly independent rather than approximately so, and carrying a multiscale second-moment computation through without tracking the coupling error terms; because the GFF is only log-correlated rather than an exact branching random walk, the independence used in the concentric decomposition is an approximation that must be explicitly controlled, and skipping this step is a common source of unjustified exponent claims for GFF level-set percolation. Canonical reference: Biskup and Louidor, 2016, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Biskup and Louidor, 2018, Advances in Mathematics; Biskup, Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes, 2020, Springer.
Discrete Gaussian free field on a two-dimensional lattice domain with Dirichlet boundary conditions
Gibbs-Markov (domain Markov) property and lattice Green function asymptotics
Random-walk-below-a-barrier (ballot) estimates for the scale walk

gaussian.title: Technique: Gibbs-Markov Property of the Gaussian Free Field
gaussian.body:
TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let h be a (discrete or continuum) Gaussian free field on a domain D with Dirichlet boundary conditions, and let U be a deterministic subdomain of D. The Gibbs-Markov (domain Markov) property states that h decomposes as h = h_U + phi_U, where h_U is a zero-boundary Gaussian free field on U, phi_U is the harmonic extension into U of the values of h on the boundary of U, h_U and phi_U are independent of each other, and phi_U is measurable with respect to the sigma-field generated by h restricted to the complement of U. This is the discrete and continuum analogue of the strong Markov property for Brownian motion and harmonic functions, and it is the fundamental tool enabling induction-on-scale arguments, the theory of local sets, and the construction of conformally invariant objects such as Liouville quantum gravity from the field. It does not hold for general non-Gibbsian or non-Gaussian log-correlated fields without separate verification, and it requires exact specification of the domain and boundary conditions, since the decomposition depends on the harmonic extension operator for the particular pair (D,U) being used. Typical failure: Applying the plain Gibbs-Markov decomposition with U chosen depending on the field h itself, such as a random subdomain determined by a level set or an exploration process, without checking that U is a valid stopping domain for the field's filtration; naively random domains destroy the independence between h_U and phi_U, and the correct fix requires the more delicate theory of local sets developed by Schramm and Sheffield, not the plain domain Markov property. Canonical reference: Sheffield, 2007, Probability Theory and Related Fields; Schramm and Sheffield, 2013, Probability Theory and Related Fields.
h is a Gaussian free field with Dirichlet (or otherwise precisely specified) boundary conditions on domain D
U is a deterministic, or at least suitably measurable stopping-domain, subdomain of D
the Green's function and harmonic measure for D and U are well defined, requiring sufficient domain regularity
correct identification of phi_U as harmonic in U with boundary values equal to h on the boundary of U

gaussian.title: Attempt on SLE4 from spectral truncations of the Gaussian free field
gaussian.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: SLE4 from spectral truncations of the Gaussian free field structural reduction or obstruction Result: Even uniform convergence of smooth functions does not make zero sets continuous. On a fixed square, h_n(x,y)=1/n has no zero set, whereas its uniform limit0 vanishes everywhere. With changing signs, n^(-1)sin(nx) also converges uniformly to0 but has many macroscopic vertical zero components. Check: The sup norms are at most1/n. For the sinusoidal example the zero lines are x=k*pi/n wherever they lie in the square; their number diverges. Obstruction: These examples do not satisfy the prescribed random-field law or boundary data; they invalidate only the proposed continuous-mapping argument. Uniform control of near-zero topology and a characterization of the selected interface are missing.
